calculation.reason: The official 1993-present annual table, current formula branches, and rate-at-entry rule are modeled, but day count, compounding, partial-payment allocation, renewal treatment, and all contract or special-judgment branches are not deterministic.

branches.general: Utah Code §15-1-4(3)(a): January 1 federal post-judgment rate plus two percentage points
branches.contract: §15-1-4(2)(a): a lawful contract judgment conforms to the contract and agreed interest rate
branches.goods_services_under_10000: §15-1-4(4): qualifying judgments under $10,000 involving goods or services use the January 1 federal rate plus ten points
branches.rate_lock: Utah Courts instructs renewal filers to use the rate in effect when the judgment was entered for the life of that judgment

annual_rate.notes: Utah State Courts publishes a 5.51% general civil and criminal judgment rate for 2026 under Utah Code §15-1-4: the federal post-judgment rate on January 1 (3.51%) plus two percentage points. A qualifying judgment under $10,000 involving goods or services instead uses 13.51% (federal rate plus ten points), while a lawful contract can supply its agreed rate. The applicable annual rate is selected when judgment is entered and remains attached to that judgment. Verify the correct branch; not legal advice.

Utah State Courts publishes a 5.51% general civil and criminal judgment rate for 2026 under Utah Code §15-1-4: the federal post-judgment rate on January 1 (3.51%) plus two percentage points. A qualifying judgment under $10,000 involving goods or services instead uses 13.51% (federal rate plus ten points), while a lawful contract can supply its agreed rate. The applicable annual rate is selected when judgment is entered and remains attached to that judgment. Verify the correct branch; not legal advice.
